(94) "The most terrible winds, agitated and violent, will tear apart that entire body; such sufferings are certain for me in hell. (95) All sentient beings shall behold my body, tormented by suffering."
For the sake of building this house, I have taken wealth belonging to others;
likewise, my sons, daughters, brother, sister,
as well as my mother, father, and the circle of my friends and kinsmen.

(97) I have wandered through the misdeeds of possessing slaves, laborers, cattle, servants, and livestock, as well as vessels of silver and gold. (98) Likewise, I have wandered in causing houses to be built with very fine garments.
Having built a most wonderful house, crowded with men and women,
and having struck the lutes and musical instruments, my mind— so difficult to tame—
was delighted; yet even now, he who was so grateful has not even anointed his body with scented waters.
(100) You are a body devoid of consciousness; I have been deluded because of you.
There is no being whatsoever who could be my protector or knowledge for me.
(101) Amidst this most terrible agitation of the winds and the torment of the body, [you alone remain].
Various delicious flavors were tasted by the tongue; likewise, many beautiful white garlands were bound upon the head. The eye was dazzled by such beauty that no protection for the eye existed.

(103) "The eyes were the cause of my sins; yet having seen [the truth], I have acted accordingly. My ears were likewise the cause for me, and my arms were struck by the thunderbolt. (104) Bracelets were bound upon my hands, and finger-rings were worn upon my fingers."
Around his neck were pearl necklaces, and his feet were well-adorned;
having fashioned lattices right there, he stood upon a golden pedestal,
while his limbs were set with various gems as well as golden bracelets.
(106) I have been delighted by noble enjoyments that gratify the mind, and I, seized by craving, have indulged in delicate touches. (107) My body has been made to sport upon various rugs and beds.
Having bathed in clear perfumed waters and been anointed with fragrant unguents, he was further incensed with divine camphor, sandalwood, and incenses;
and his complexion-enhancing garment was prepared by being blended with musk.
(109) Anointed with *gandhavārṣika* oil and [garlands of] *sumanā*, *caṇpaka*, and other flowers, and wearing a white garment made of fine *kāśika* silk;
(110) having descended from the back of an elephant and mounted the back of a horse.
"I consider myself a king; people run before me. I know the inner apartments well, being highly trained in song and dance.
Yet, innocent deer have been killed by my arrows during the hunt."
(112) Such evil was committed by me, ignorant of the next world; I ate the flesh of others, and therefore this suffering is mine.
(113) "I did not know that this terrible death would come; I was of childish intellect, and I nourished only this body.
(114) Death has now come upon me, and no savior is to be found."
For you are all my kinsmen; why do you gaze at my face?
(115) Why do you tear your clothes, and for what reason do you lament?
Why do you dishevel your hair? What can blood possibly do?
(116) Why do you throw dust upon your heads and beat your breasts? I am not to be restrained from living; what is the use of your weeping?
(117) My body is the food for wolves, dogs, and crows.
This body, nourished in vain by birds,
will become like one touched by the serpent of death;
therefore, one should employ medicine in such a way that one is liberated from this fear.
(119) Whatever medicine the physicians may give me is not desired by me now; what is required is the medicine of the Dharma, which liberates one from the serpents of the afflictions.
(120) It must be given to me while I am still alive; do not bestow it upon me when I am dead.
This body, which must inevitably perish even while being nourished—
why do I project this mass of evil that will later yield only suffering?
This beloved body, once nurtured by me, will only act with ingratitude.

(122) "O sons and daughter, why do you gaze upon me with such [pained] eyes? Save me from this disease; why do you weep so pointlessly? For you, my sons and daughter, have now become ungrateful toward me. (123)
I have taken what belongs to others for the sake of nourishing you;
now that I have met with death, why do you leave me hopeless?
I am terrified by the miserable states of rebirth and tormented by death.
(125) Sensation, perception, mental formations, contact, and supreme sensations—
the fool is led astray by craving and reaps a bitter fruit;
(126) for me, born into an unfortunate family, there is the bond of sorrow.
But knowing me to be of little merit, other people will grieve for me—
fallen from generosity and morality, turned away from the Dharma, and afflicted by the venom of the serpent of the afflictions, unaware of rebirth. (127)
(128) The fool is led astray by ignorance where liberation does not exist;
deluded, he does not understand the purpose of liberation and commits evil deeds.
(129) The fool, whose mind is constantly distracted, is perpetually led astray by the afflictions.
For this body, bound by various fetters, is consumed by blazing fire;
the body wanders in confusion where no happiness is found, and it does not know that happiness which brings ultimate bliss. (130)
The field of the Buddhas bestows happiness; the Wheel of Dharma is the great medicine; morality and truth are the ornaments of those who observe discipline; and the Tathāgatas are the Brahma-voice.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena and said this: "In this way, Bhaiṣajyasena, beings lament at the time of death;
yet there will be no savior for them, other than the ripening of the fruit of their well-performed deeds. And he spoke these verses:
Having indeed committed evil deeds, they fall into the hells;
there they eat glowing embers and drink molten iron.
Embers rain down upon their bodies, and being scorched, they cry out piteously.
In this most terrifying hell, their bodies are consumed by fire;
they do not recognize happiness, nor do they understand the Dharma.
The fool wanders about through unrighteousness and attains no happiness whatsoever.
(135) Endowed with faith and ethical conduct, possessed of wisdom, and great in austerity,
one who cultivates virtuous friends will quickly become a Tathāgata.
(136) One exerts vigor for the sake of the higher good, in order to be reborn in the world of the Buddhas.
"Teach the wholesome Dharma that embraces all sentient beings;
having entered a mind of loving-kindness and being devoted to the holy life,
Bhaiṣajyasena, upon hearing this, you should be intent on its practice."
(138) That which is called the mind of awakening (bodhicitta) is the Buddha who reveals liberation, the Leader whose voice is most excellent, and the mother and father of the world.
(139) It is the supreme spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) who teaches that which is extremely difficult to perform.
In this world of Dharma, those who listen to the teaching of the Buddha with reverence shall become Buddhas, Sugatas, the supreme among men;
they shall become Lords of the World, the liberators of all sentient beings. (140)
Those who possess reverence for the peaceful Buddha-fields.
[SaSū 245] Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, why does this earth tremble and shake so violently?
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena: “Look, Bhaiṣajyasena; what do you see?
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena looked.
Then, at that very moment, he sees from the four directions;
the earth opens up a fissure,
and as the earth is opened, he beholds it.
From the fissures of the earth, twenty koṭis of humans are born;
in the downward direction, twenty koṭis of humans are born;
and in the upward direction, twenty-five koṭis of humans are born.

[SaSū 246] Then those young beings, having looked toward the Blessed One, said this to him: "Blessed One, who are these born here? The Blessed One said: "Do you see these multitudes of people? They replied: "We see them, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: "These multitudes of people were born as your friends. They said: "Blessed One, will there also be death for these beings?"
The Blessed One said: "It is even so, friends; all sentient beings will likewise face death.

Then those former beings who were young and had been born first approached the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence and said this to him: "O Blessed One, we do not venture to undergo birth and death again."
The Blessed One said, "Do you have the resolve to behold that which is obtained through the power of heroism?

They replied, "We would wish to see the Tathāgata face to face, and in his presence hear the sweet and pleasing teaching of the Dharma; we would wish to see the community of the Tathāgata’s disciples seated there, and we would wish to see the Bodhisattvas of great supernatural power and great majesty. And yet, O Blessed One, we do not have the resolve for such a thing."
In order to behold birth and death,

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena then rose from his seat by the power of his supernatural faculties, together with those five hundred Bodhisattvas; they all rose by means of their supernatural powers and walked back and forth in the sky above.
Having assumed the cross-legged posture, they meditate;
from all their bodies, lions emerge and tigers emerge.
Vipers emerge;
elephants emerge;
they display great miraculous transformations.
And having fashioned couches upon the mountains, they sit there;
they ascend twenty thousand yojanas upward,
and ten thousand times ten million suns and moons descend.

[SaSū 249] Then those young beings said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for this great radiance of light rays and this great manifestation of miraculous power that has appeared in the world?
The Blessed One said: "Noble sons, behold these two, the moon and the sun, who have appeared."
They said, "We see it, Blessed One; we see it, Sugata.

The Blessed One said, "This radiance of light rays and miraculous display of supernatural power have been shown by the Bodhisattvas from their own bodies; having displayed them, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings."
For the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, and for the sake, welfare, and happiness of the great mass of people—
both gods and humans— they have displayed the power of vigor within this very human body and manifested such power of supernatural transformation (*ṛddhi*).
He said:
"May the Blessed One teach the Dharma for the manifestation of the appearance of light rays.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena: "Bhaiṣajyasena, do you see this trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world-system?"
The earth shook in six ways, and he said:
"I see it, Blessed One; I see it, Sugata. O Blessed One, this thought occurred to me: 'I should ask the Tathāgata about this matter.'"

The Blessed One said: "Ask, Bhaiṣajyasena, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question. I shall explain, analyze, and, Bhaiṣajyasena, I shall reveal all that pertains to the past, future, and present times.
He said:
May the Blessed One teach me for the sake of dispelling my remorse.
Here, Blessed One, I see the Tathāgata surrounded by eighty-four thousand sons of gods, surrounded by eighty-four thousand koṭis of bodhisattvas,
and surrounded by twelve thousand koṭis of nāga kings.
He was surrounded by eighteen thousand koṭis of bhūtas and surrounded by twenty-five thousand koṭis of pretas and piśācas.
The Blessed One said: "Bhaiṣajyasena, these beings who have gathered and are seated here in this assembly to hear the Dharma from me—Bhaiṣajyasena, they shall today turn their backs upon saṃsāra."
This very day they shall attain the ten stages;
established in the ten stages, they shall reach the realm of Nirvana.

Seeking the welfare of all beings, having performed the Dharma for the sake of liberating others from old age and death, and bringing happiness, they shall conquer the snare of the afflictions and attain the teaching of the Buddha.
He asked: "Blessed One, have these beings, who occupy many different stations of existence, arisen through various and diverse karmas?
They stand surrounding the Blessed One."
The Blessed One said: "Listen, Bhaiṣajyasena. He replied:
"Deluded beings do not know from where liberation will come."
Many new beings will today attain dhāraṇī;
they shall come to know all dharmas for the sake of attaining the ten stages,
and having attained those ten stages, they will perform the work of a Buddha.
(143) They shall turn the wheel of Dharma and rain down the rain of Dharma;
my teaching is delightful, and by it sentient beings have gathered—
(144) gods, nāgas, pretas, and even the most formidable asuras.
Struck by the sound of the Dharma, they shall be established on the ten stages; sounding the drum of the Dharma and filling the conch of the Dharma,
today these nine beings will possess the power of vigor.
(146) Today these beings shall attain the Dharma just as it was attained by the Tathāgatas.
[SaSū 252] Then, about five thousand young beings rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
(147) "O Blessed One, this body is a heavy burden and is cruel and full of great terror;
by it we are bound in saṃsāra, not knowing its end."
(148) We do not recognize the path, for the path itself is not seen. O Protector, we have become blind; please take us under your care.
(149) We entreat you, O Hero: teach the Dharma, O Leader!
"We were born with little wisdom and are indeed ignorant of happiness. Teach us the Dharma and deliver us from this terrible suffering,
so that wherever we may be reborn, there may be for us the sight of a Buddha."
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena approached those young beings; having approached them, he addressed those young beings with a verse:
(151) "Eat your food, drink this wonderful juice, and afterwards, having become confident, you shall hear the Dharma without fear."
They said:
"Venerable Elder, we do not know who you are;
we see that you are gracious, of peaceful appearance, and of great renown."
(153) You have been liberated from the great terror of the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts; all your sins have been pacified, so that you shine resplendent in the world.
(154) We see in your hand a water-pot endowed with the seven precious jewels.
The Sūtra, composed of jewels, is coiled around your body like a mass of radiance;
we were unable to carry it away. We have no need for food, nor do we desire delicious drink. Your words are peaceful.
(156) From food, excrement arises, and likewise from drink, urine;
blood comes from the essence (*rasa*), and from the blood, flesh is produced.
(157) We have no need for food or for well-prepared drinks.
They should not wear fine garments made of silk or fine cotton,
nor should they have golden bracelets or pearl necklaces;
they should not even wear rings, for all of them are constant followers of dharma.
(159) We seek life itself and would not go to an evil rebirth; we seek the gift of Dharma, even more than the pleasures of the gods.
(160) One should cultivate the state of a spiritual friend, not the sovereignty of universal monarchs.
The universal monarchs will die, leaving behind their most beautiful continents;
neither sons follow behind them, nor wives, nor daughters;
even the seven jewels turn back and shall not go after them.

(162) Having assembled a great multitude of people, they do not turn their backs, nor do they run ahead; they no longer remain under [his] control. (163) Kings who have only one more birth remaining have been led astray many times by constant [delusion].
Having committed sinful deeds, they fall into the Raurava hell.
Having wandered in all four directions with the seven great and powerful jewels,
where will that supernatural power go when one dwells in Raurava?
(165) Having died, they are unable to exercise supernatural power where the earth no longer exists;
O Elder, listen to us: go where the Tathāgata is.
(166) For we long for a vision of him, just as a mother and father do.
We have no mother, no father, and no brothers;
the Tathāgata alone is the teacher of the world, our mother and our father,
and he is both the moon and the sun who reveals the path of security.
(168) For he is the liberator from cyclic existence, by whom one is not born again; he is the non-further-crosser over the flood, the flood of afflictions, and the great terror.
(169) By him sentient beings have been ferried across, so that they shall never again turn back.
The True Dharma was taught by him for the sake of supreme enlightenment;
we have no need for food, nor do we desire the fruits of kingship, nor is it our aim to go to the world of the gods, as we are terrified of hell.
(171) A human birth is seen to be pleasant where the All-Knowing One appears;
yet those with short lifespans are seen due to their own misdeeds.
(172) They are attached to sensual enjoyments and do not perceive death.
They do not know and they do not fear, being devoid of [the understanding of] cessation and arising;
they do not know subtle phenomena and they do not perform subtle actions;
with minds overcome by ignorance, they do not know the peaceful realm.
(174) Passing away, they do not grow weary, yet they are born again and again; for a long time, struck by suffering, they are beaten by the rod of impermanence.
(175) They will seize what belongs to others, and likewise they are slain and bound.
Bound by the five fetters and impelled by their former misdeeds, they will die devoid of hope, pierced by the arrows of grief;
as their consciousness ceases, they lament piteously.
(177) Who indeed might be my protector? I shall give away all my enjoyments;
I shall offer gold, silver, and crystal, and I shall even become a slave. (178) I shall perform every task that is worthy of a servant.
"I have no need for royal power or enjoyments, nor for grain or wealth;
I have need only of my own body, for one who commits evil is never released.
Thus, O Elder, there would be no food for us."
(180) Even kings will die, though they have enjoyed exquisite food;
even sons of gods will die, though they have drunk the most excellent drink, (181) that prepared food and drink endowed with various flavors.
Having brought food before him, the king touches it with his tongue;
for kings, greedy for flavors, commit no small amount of evil. They take delight in impermanent tastes, wherein no essence is to be found.

(183) We must not drink, nor indeed must we eat; such is the nature of reality that we should practice so that we may be liberated from suffering. (184) [It is] the liberation from the bond of craving, the release from the affliction of craving.

We have gone for refuge to that Buddha who is liberated from all bonds. Indeed, we go for refuge to the Great Seer, the Lord of the World; we go to pay homage to him whose appearance is dear to all beings. (185)
(186) “We do not know your name; tell us your auspicious name.
The Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasena said:
“Indeed, you all wish to hear the name of every person.”
(187) Surrounded by nine hundred thousand crores of beings, the Tathāgata was addressed as follows: "We wish to hear your name, which arises from all virtues.
(188) "Your name is heard to be profound; you are a disciple of the Buddhas. He replied:
"I am Bhaiṣajyasena by name; indeed, I am the medicine for sentient beings. I shall teach you all the supreme medicine that pacifies every disease, for the sake of people afflicted by every ailment."

(190) Passion is a disease, a great disease that perishes in the world, a terrible affliction; delusion is a most horrific disease by which the unintelligent wander. (191) Indeed, beings go to hell, as well as to the realms of animals and hungry ghosts.
These fools are seized by hatred; how can there be peace for them?
They said:
"Having heard this auspicious Dharma, may we be liberated from all suffering;
yet those of childish intellect and ignorant minds remain unliberated from all sufferings."
(193) Free from evil deeds, we shall hear the gift of Dharma; having abandoned all evil, with fear and terror utterly destroyed,
(194) we shall quickly behold the Perfectly Awakened One, the liberator from all diseases.
To the King of Physicians, the Great Physician, the healer of those who suffer— (195) go quickly, Elder, to pay homage to the Tathāgata;
and in our name, offer salutations to the Guide of the World and speak to him.
(196) Quench this disease; quench this most dreadful fire, for this entire body is ablaze and, being consumed, finds no peace.
(197) O you of noble vows, show compassion toward us who are tormented by suffering.
The burden of the body is a great burden, a sharp burden, most terrible;
overcome by hatred and delusion, people always carry it.
Again and again these ignorant ones carry this burden, yet they do not carry the burden of liberation.
(199) They do not realize they must die, and thus no fear arises in them.
Not knowing the path to liberation and failing to see the path to liberation, (200) they remain complacent, thinking, "Death shall never come to us."
Agitated, they do not recognize even as they behold their mother dead;
others do not remember their father, being constantly tormented by disease and overwhelmed by afflictions and karma— how can we eat our food?
(202) We do not know the end of suffering, yet we labor in vain;
such sufferings as ours arise from the cause of ignorance regarding birth.
(203) There is great fear and a heavy burden: perception, mental formations, and sensation.

The fool who does not understand the Dharma is led astray by craving. Born indeed for the sake of misfortune in this world, burdened by the weight of the body, he thinks there is need for bathing and ointments, for clean clothes, and for beautiful finery.
(205) One should prepare delicious food that is pleasing to the body,
and likewise request the five musical instruments for the ear;
(206) the eyes take delight in forms arising from the seven precious gems.
The tongue even begs for every kind of delicious and savory taste;
the body always craves soft and subtle touch;
and pleasure arises from the two kinds of flesh being pressed together by the body.

(208) For this body is indeed insentient; who could find delight therein? My feet find pleasure there because they are covered by beautiful leather. (209) Neither clothing nor ointments provide protection against death.
The body would not be a protection; how much less so clothing and ointments?
It is said that the person is the body; the breath is its great strength and sharp power. One should discern that within that body there is a great quality.
(211) Formerly, surrounded by horses and elephants, I was made to wander about in sport; ignorant of the Dharma of Liberation, I delighted in evil deeds.
(212) Out of mere playfulness, and unaware of the next world, I caused sinful acts to be committed.
Again and again I was born, and again and again I encountered death; grief was seen again and again, along with the bondage of lamentation.
The death of mothers was witnessed, and fathers dead were seen as well.
(214) Kinsmen, sisters, sons, and even a wife who has died—all conditioned phenomena are indeed empty. For what conscious person would take delight in them?
(215) Indeed, I realized that trust was placed [in them] by my mind, which had been seized by greed.
I did not perceive the peaceful Dharma, nor did I rejoice in death;
therefore, with a mind shrouded by greed, I gave no gift.
What evil could be equal to greed, which even now does not turn back?
(217) We have indeed become bewildered, and the entire world is bewildered; bewildered, we hear a sound that is the embrace of false dharmas.
(218) We seek liberation and meditations, yet we do not sustain our bodies.
"May we become Buddhas for the sake of the world, teachers and gurus in the universe! The Buddha is the mother and father in the world; the Buddha is the one who reveals the path.
He rains down the rain of Dharma everywhere throughout Jambudvīpa."
(220) Deluded beings do not know how the gathering of phenomena occurs;
having directed the mind toward awakening, the gathering of phenomena is attained.
(221) All conditioned formations are empty; enjoyments and wealth are likewise empty.
Seeing ourselves empty, we have become despondent. O Elder Bhaiṣajyasena, listen to our words:
for the sake of the bodhisattvas, we would cast ourselves far away.
(223) The Bodhisattvas, endowed with vigor and great austerity, do not grow weary; remembering the faults of saṃsāra, they gather together virtuous qualities.
(224) Go where that Teacher is and ask on our behalf.
The Teacher, the Jina, having attained bliss, may he not suffer in the slightest;
Māra, together with his army and his mounts, has been defeated by you.
You have swiftly kindled the Dharma that brings happiness to all sentient beings.
(226) "Nor have we heard the Dharma by which we might become Buddhas. Go quickly, Elder, for the sake of our welfare!
(227) We shall not cross over as long as we do not see the Tathāgata."
All stood there with reverence before him who bore the thirty-two marks.
The Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasena said:
"Look upward for a moment; what do you see right now?
They looked upward while standing there, and there were no fewer than five [beings].
Three hundred thousand gabled pavilions were situated all around,
constructed of the seven precious gems and beautifully adorned with nets of jewels;
in their center was a full-blown lotus emitting a divine fragrance.
(231) There they ask the Elder, "What is this that is seen here— these gabled chambers with jeweled lattices, resting upon the filaments of lotuses?
Bhaiṣajyasena said:
(232) These are your stations; go to behold the Buddha! Pay homage to that Light of the World, who is the transcendent Teacher.
They said:
"In that regard, we do not know and do not see the path [to] the Tathāgata;
since we do not know the path, where shall we go to pay him homage?"
Bhaiṣajyasena said:
"One must go to pay homage to the Teacher, whose radiance is like nectar;
yet he cannot be grasped, being as infinite as space."
(235) This Teacher stands in his place, just as the Merus stand;
he is like Sumeru and like the deep foundation of the great ocean.
And from the arising of the Buddha's wisdom, there is no dust even within a trichiliocosm.
The Illuminator of the World was honored by Bodhisattvas in the ten directions.
They said:
"Look upon us, O Lord of the World; fulfill our aspiration! We have paid homage to the Teacher with our minds, and from that we have obtained the fruit."
The Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasena said:
"The Teacher is not attached to perfumes, nor to garlands, nor to ointments;
he grasps the cause for the sake of sentient beings by which they are liberated from the conditioned."
Māra shall not wage a most dreadful battle against him who has tamed his mind and gone for refuge to the Buddha;
he shall not fall under the power of death and shall swiftly attain the dhāraṇī.
Having attained clarity of mind, he then beheld the Teacher.
Thereupon, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata whose voice is as pleasant as the song of the kalaviṅka bird, manifested a smile.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena rose from his seat and extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One.

Having prostrated before the Blessed One, he said this: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of this smile, such that from the Blessed One’s mouth eighty-four hundred thousand rays of light issue forth?
By these rays, this great trichiliocosm has been filled with radiance, all thirty-two great hells have been filled, and the thirty-two celestial palaces have been illuminated."

And those rays were of various colors— namely, blue, yellow, red, white, madder-red, crystal, silver, and gold— and having issued from the Blessed One’s mouth, they provided every form of relief to sentient beings throughout the triple-thousand great thousandfold world system; then, returning once more, they circumambulated the Blessed One seven times.
They vanished into the crown of the Blessed One’s head.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena said this to the Blessed One:
"I would like to ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, about a certain matter."
If the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity, I would ask a question for the sake of receiving an answer.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena: "Ask, Bhaiṣajyasena, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind by answering each and every question you ask.
When this had been said, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"O Blessed One, thirty thousand koṭis of young beings have appeared who penetrate the subtle teaching of the Dharma of the Tathāgata;
yet, O Blessed One, they revile, disparage, and oppress the subtle [teaching] of the elder beings."

"You are not aged beings who understand the Dharma; you always delight in what is unrighteous and unwholesome. Therefore, why do they speak such smooth and pleasing words to the Blessed One? The Blessed One said: "Bhaiṣajyasena, do you not know for what reason these beings speak such words?"
Having heard this gentle and well-spoken Dharma taught by the Tathāgata, Bhaiṣajyasena, they will realize the meaning of all phenomena and will become endowed with all virtuous qualities;
and they shall all penetrate the dhāraṇīs.
From this day forward, they shall be established upon the ten stages;
today they shall sound the great drum;
today they shall be endowed with the great modes of Dharma.
"Bhaiṣajyasena, do you see these gabled pavilions?"
Bhaiṣajyasena said, "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, Sugata.
The Blessed One said, "Today, Bhaiṣajyasena, these young beings, having ascended into these gabled palaces, will attain the realization of the Dharma.
Today, they will bring all wholesome qualities to complete fulfillment."
Today they shall beat the great drum of the Dharma;
today there will be the realization of the Dharma for many hosts of devas;
and for many beings who have set out toward the miserable states of existence, upon hearing this teaching of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, there will be a total turning away from and defeat of all saṃsāra.
And at that time, ninety-nine billion elder beings will all attain the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpatti-phala*), and they shall be endowed with all dharmas.
Bhaiṣajyasena, they shall all be completely freed from all suffering.
Bhaiṣajyasena, they will all accomplish the vision of all the Tathāgatas;
Bhaiṣajyasena, they will all be endowed with the Great Dharma.
Look around, Bhaiṣajyasena, in the four directions!

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena looked all around in the four directions; he saw that from the eastern direction fifty *koṭis* of Bodhisattvas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, were coming;
from the southern direction sixty *koṭis* of Bodhisattvas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, were coming.
From the western direction, Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of seventy *koṭis* of Ganges rivers arrive;
from the northern direction, Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of eighty *koṭis* of Ganges rivers arrive;
and from the downward direction, Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of nine thousand *koṭis* of Ganges rivers arrive.
From the upward direction, hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, arrived.
As those bodhisattva mahāsattvas arrived one after another, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One before him and sat to one side.
Then, to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had come from the ten directions and were seated to one side, Bhaiṣajyasena—
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is this black form and red form that I see in the sky among the birds?
The Blessed One said: "What is this, Bhaiṣajyasena?"
"You do not recognize that which you see in the sky as a black form and a red form.
He replied, "I do not know it, Blessed One; I do not know it, Sugata."
The Blessed One said: "Only the Tathāgata knows this.
Bhaiṣajyasena, this is Māra who has approached here for the purpose of causing blindness. Bhaiṣajyasena, do you wish to see these bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are stationed in the midst of the sky?
He replied: "I do."
"I desire it, Blessed One; I desire it, Sugata.
Then the Blessed One, having revealed those bodhisattvas, addressed the bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena:
"Bhaiṣajyasena, hundreds of millions of bodhisattvas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, have arrived in such a manner."
He asked: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, that so many of these bodhisattvas have come here?
The Blessed One said: "Bhaiṣajyasena, it is for the sake of young beings; now all beings will become endowed with the meditative concentration on the Dharma."
"Bhaiṣajyasena, do you see these bodhisattvas mahāsattvas of various forms who have arrived through the empowerment of their supernatural power?

He replied, "I have beheld world-systems as numerous as the sands of a hundred billion Ganges rivers; therein I have seen bodhisattvas mahāsattvas as numerous as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges rivers, each abiding by his own supernatural power, of various forms and various colors."
They abide in various powers and configurations;
those bodhisattvas abide in the dwellings of the noble dharmas,
and their retinues of bodhisattvas abide in the dwellings of the dharmas.

The Blessed One having spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvaśūra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasena, all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas— both those newly arrived and those long-established—
and the entire assembly, including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
